**Allowed browser origins**

The `origin` callback passed to `cors()` in `worker/src/index.ts:19-31` decides this. It applies to every route through `app.use('*', …)`. It returns the request's origin if any of these match:

- `origin === 'http://localhost:4200'` (exact match, for local Angular dev).
- `origin.endsWith('.pages.dev')`, which matches any depth.
- `origin.endsWith('.workers.dev')`, which matches any depth. The deployed frontend, `https://ai-dnd-frontend.ai-dnd.workers.dev`, is allowed this way.

Anything else gets `null`, so no CORS headers are sent and the browser blocks the call. A request with no `Origin` header also gets `null`. That includes curl and server-to-server calls, which aren't affected by CORS in any case.

The same `cors()` call also sets these values:
- `allowMethods`: GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS
- `allowHeaders`: Content-Type, Authorization
- `maxAge`: 86400

I read the methods, headers and `maxAge` from the copy of this block in `docs/DEPLOYMENT_NOTES.md` §4. I didn't open the lines below 31 in `index.ts`, so check them there if it matters.

**Where to add a custom domain**

Add a condition inside the `if (...)` in that `origin` function, next to the other `origin === …` and `.endsWith(…)` checks:

```ts
origin === 'https://play.example.com' ||
```

- Use the full origin (scheme + host, no trailing slash) with an exact `===` match. Use `endsWith` only if you want every subdomain of that domain allowed.
- Don't put the domain into an array or use a `*` wildcard. Hono treats array entries as literal strings, so wildcards never match (`docs/DEPLOYMENT_NOTES.md` §4).
- `worker/wrangler.toml` doesn't need changing for CORS.
- Per AGENTS.md §6, update the CORS line in `worker/src/index.md` and the code sample in `docs/DEPLOYMENT_NOTES.md` §4 in the same change.

I also haven't checked how the frontend picks its API URL. That's in `frontend/src/environments/environment.md`, and it's a separate setting from CORS.
